findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-identical to the default light view; the probe reports color-scheme: normal, a white body background, and zero prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define surface, text, link, and control colours with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme media query.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly instead of preserving visual continuity.
findings.evidence: Homepage, category, and detail navigation are full document transitions; the CSS probe found zero view-transition rules and no transition names.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared header and selected-card imagery, while retaining reduced-motion behaviour.

findings.summary: Brand chrome and empty space push the listing content below the first mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360×800, the header, 11 category buttons, large logo, and whitespace consume roughly the first 650 px; the first content card begins near the bottom of the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Compress the header and logo block on narrow screens, collapse secondary categories into a disclosure, and bring the first content card and primary action into the initial viewport.

findings.guidanceId: touch target size hover fallback pointer input focus-visible
findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and some important controls are shorter than the recommended touch target.
findings.evidence: Programmatic keyboard-style focus matched :focus-visible but computed outline was none and box-shadow none; detail server controls measured 33 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible outline that is not removed, and increase server/control hit areas to at least 44 CSS px without reducing the visible label.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable render-blocking and unused CSS/JavaScript despite otherwise strong load metrics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 62 KiB unused CSS and 67 KiB unused JavaScript. HAR shows two parser-blocking stylesheets (about 66 KiB total) and a 95.6 KiB script as the largest transfer; Lighthouse estimates 150 ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused Bootstrap/theme rules and unused script features, split page-specific assets, and inline or preload only genuinely critical CSS while deferring the rest.

findings.summary: The last-page pagination link’s accessible name does not include its visible label.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified a.last with visible text “Last »” but aria-label “Last Page”, failing WCAG 2.5.3 label-in-name.
findings.suggestedFix: Use visible Thai text as the accessible name, or make aria-label include the exact visible “Last” wording rather than replacing it.

findings.summary: The primary prerecorded video exposes no caption track or equivalent.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found the ready primary video with trackCount 0; no captions or transcript were visible in the detail-page evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide synchronised WebVTT captions via <track kind="captions"> and a transcript or equivalent for meaningful audio; ensure the custom player exposes caption controls.

findings.summary: Listing images lack intrinsic dimensions and responsive source selection, and several use legacy JPEG delivery.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 20/20 without width/height, 20/20 without srcset, 20 below-fold images without native loading=lazy, and 9 legacy-format images. Lighthouse also flagged a 407 px image displayed at 402 px as under-resolved for high-density screens.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height, responsive srcset/sizes, native loading=lazy for below-fold cards, and AVIF/WebP variants with a sufficiently sharp candidate for high-density screens.

findings.summary: HTTPS is present, but the response omits the browser’s core defensive headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, a strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; test before enforcing CSP.

findings.summary: All observed analytics cookies are sent without Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.evidence: The cookie audit found seven 365-day first-party cookies; all seven had Secure=false, HttpOnly=false, and SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark cookies Secure and choose SameSite=Lax or Strict unless cross-site delivery is essential; shorten analytics retention and avoid setting unnecessary identifiers.

findings.summary: A third-party analytics integration creates persistent identifiers without any visible consent or privacy control.
findings.evidence: HAR and tracker evidence show requests to s10.histats.com and s4.histats.com; the resulting seven analytics-style cookies persist for 365 days. No consent overlay or control appeared in load screenshots.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove Histats unless it is necessary; otherwise gate it behind meaningful consent, reduce collection and retention, batch events, and document the data flow.
